reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: I read CONTEXT.txt whole first (the “Working with your guards” section; the draft sits once, at the end of the third paragraph, right after “It's what protects you when your consciously installed parental Protector isn't functioning, the same as when you were a child.”), then DRAFT.txt, SOURCE.txt and the_change. CHANGE CHECK: the draft is Emulate's two sentences (sample ck) in place of the card's two: ask what it is trying to stop or what it wants before deciding what it is; it may be the child, the script, the day, or a mix. Its last words are the approved card's “or a bit of each”, as the_change says, not Emulate's “or a combination”. MEANING CHECK against IC-A14 (“But before you decide where it's coming from, ask it what it's trying to stop, or what it wants. It could also be your inner child, mad that you took so long to come back, or your inherited parent script, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each.”): every point is there in the same order: ask first (“what it is trying to stop or what it wants”), before labelling it; then the possibilities (the inner child mad that it has taken you so long to come back; the inherited parent script; something from earlier in the day; a bit of each). No claim or fact is added. Small turns I weighed and accept: “decide where it's coming from” became “figuring out what/where it is” (the slash is the one slightly odd spot, but “where is it” is ordinary parts-work talk, the section opens with “Feel free to use parts language here”, and the list that follows answers what it is, so the sense holds); the leading “But” and the “also” are gone (“of course” does the same job of conceding the inner child as one candidate, and it calls back the paragraph above that warns against expecting to find your inner child); “ask it” became “ask what it is…” (the next paragraph speaks to the guard directly, so who is asked is clear); “make sure to” is a touch more coaching than his bare “ask” but carries the same instruction. SEAM CHECK: read in the paragraph it follows from the guard sentence and keeps his own long comma-and-“or” list style (the same paragraph has his “numb, cynical, angry, hungry…” list, and his “or… or… or” chain comes two paragraphs later), and “mad that it’s taken you so long to come back” has a human edge. I did not hear a different writer, a hedge he wouldn't write or a tidy summary. The pronoun “it” is the reaction or guard exactly as in the card, so the draft brings no referent problem that the source did not already have there. TELL ROWS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 against the literal draft in its context and found none actually happening. Closest calls: T15 (the swaps are ordinary phrases and a few padded ones, not rare-word substitutions; it is Emulate's rewrite by design, with the card's own ending put back); T07 and T22 (“of course” and “make sure to” are single mild markers that each carry a real turn or step, not stage directions or reassurance alone); T12, T17 and T29 (the child, script, day and mix list is the card's own open enumeration of what a reaction may be, with an open slot and a catch-all, not matched A/B packaging or a closing moral); T02 (the paragraph's teaching beats are his and unchanged, and the draft keeps the same two jobs as the sentences it replaces); T26 (the “what it is / what it wants” echo is the point, and “it may be” returns after a long appositive); T20 (it ends on the catch-all “a bit of each”, not a polished closer). C01 to C04: the inner child is “your inner child”, no invented first-person fact, no outside claim. LINTER FINDINGS: “B4/E15 list or packed sentence” is accepted: the long sentence is one job, a list of genuine alternatives, it is the approved card's content so nothing can be dropped, and the paragraph's own voice runs long comma lists. “D9 follows the source order” is accepted: the only natural order is ask first, then the possibilities, and the second sentence notices something (the child mad at how long you took), so T13 and T09 are absent. The E125 list-of-three finding is accepted: the three sources and “a bit of each” are the approved card's meaning (dropping one would lose approved content), the items have different shapes (the child with its clause, “it may be” for the script, a bare phrase) and the list ends on a catch-all, which is the fix the label itself names. Verdict PASS: it does what the_change says, keeps the card's meaning, adds nothing, and reads right in its context.
resolved_lint_labels: E125 list of three: an AI pattern in general (Joel 2026-10-03: "lists of 3 in general are an ai pattern"; 2026-10-07: "lists in general are overused by AI. try to avoid that unless it's really needed"). If the meaning doesn't need all three, drop the one that matters least; if it does, split them into sentences, the way he fixed P1 ("Maybe it just has something to say."), or give the items different shapes and end on a catch-all, the way he fixed Borrowed Adulthood P2 ("Other jobs can go to friends or community, outsource to the tools or pros, whatever works.").
